# `silk/io/logger_native`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Native providers of the `Logger` effect: `StderrLogger` writes log lines to standard error,
and `StdoutLogger` writes the bare messages to standard output.

## When to use
Provide `StderrLogger` for `Logger` in a native program. It is the normal choice for
diagnostics, because it keeps the log out of the program output. Provide `StdoutLogger` when
the messages are the output of the program. Code that logs uses `silk.io.logger`, so a test can
provide `InMemoryLogger` instead.

## Details
`StderrLogger` writes one line for each message: the level, a colon and a space, the formatted
message, and a newline, such as `warning: disk 91% full`. It holds the standard error lock of
`silk.io.writer_native` for the whole line, so lines of different threads do not mix. It formats into a
buffer of 64 bytes on the stack. Thus a short line is one system call, and the logger does not
allocate.

`StderrLogger.make` colors the level name when standard error is a terminal, the `NO_COLOR`
environment variable is not set or is empty, and `TERM` is not `dumb`. It checks once, at the
first message. `StderrLogger.withColor` turns color on or off without a check.

`StdoutLogger` formats each message directly to standard output. It adds no level, timestamp,
or newline, has no lock, and does not allocate.

## Errors
`LogError` with code 3 if the write fails. Part of the message can be written already.

## Gotchas
- The providers exist on Windows x86_64 MSVC, WASI, Darwin on aarch64, and Linux with GNU libc
  on x86_64 or aarch64. Windows needs no CRT and automatic color enables console ANSI processing.
- A message template for `StderrLogger` must not end with a newline. The logger adds one.
- `StderrLogger.make` reads the environment at the first message. A change to `NO_COLOR` after
  that has no effect on the same logger.

## Examples
### Log to standard error
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.logger { LogError, Logger }
import silk.io.logger_native { StderrLogger }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! LogError {
  let mut logger = StderrLogger.make()
  let values = .{ name: "silk", count: 3 }

  // Writes "info: silk started 3 workers" and a newline to standard error.
  run Effect.logInfo("{name} started {count} workers", &values)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Logger>(&mut logger)
  return 0
}
```

### Log to standard output
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.logger { LogError, Logger }
import silk.io.logger_native { StdoutLogger }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! LogError {
  let mut logger = StdoutLogger.make()
  let values = .{ name: "silk", count: 3 }

  // The logger adds no newline, so the template ends with one.
  run Effect.logInfo("{name} started {count} workers\n", &values)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Logger>(&mut logger)
  return 0
}
```

WASI does not define terminal detection; automatic color selection is disabled on that target.
